Definition: watch, i.e. the act (custody), or (concretely) the sentry, the post; objectively preservation, or (concretely) safe; figuratively observance, i.e. (abstractly) duty or (objectively) a usage or party
BiblicalUsage: The word is the charge, the keeping, and it belongs to obedience itself. Abraham kept God's charge, His commandments and His laws; the lamb was kept up until the fourteenth day; the people kept the charge of the LORD when the cloud tarried; and Aaron and his sons were told to keep the charge of the LORD at the door of the tabernacle, that they die not.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the charge is the shape of faithfulness. Keeping is not a single act but a watch, held day after day, until the cloud moves or the seven days are done.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
